title: The Field Bench
summary: Tune a probe in a field you can see drifting, add fields at a point, steer ink drops onto paper and read particle tracks.
subject: physics
concepts: Force on a test charge, F = qE
Charged particle in a uniform field
learningOutcome: The student can find the field of one or two charges, the force on a test charge, how a charged particle moves in a uniform field, and read sign and charge-to-mass ratio from tracks.

levels.title: Probe the field
levels.adds: Baseline: the field of a point charge, E = kQ/r², and the force F = qE on a test charge (Ex 1.8b).
hints: E = k Q / r². Solve for r, with Q in coulombs and r in metres.
The field points away from a positive charge and towards a negative one.
A negative test charge feels a force opposite to the field.

levels.title: Two charges, one point
levels.adds: New idea: add the fields of two charges as vectors at a point, then find the test charge's force (Ex 1.8, Example 1.8).
hints: Find the field of each charge at P on its own, with its direction, then add them as vectors.
At the midpoint between a + and a − charge the two fields point the same way and add.
Then F = qE: a positive test charge is pushed along the field, a negative one against it.

levels.title: Ink-jet printer
levels.adds: New idea: a charged drop in a uniform field has acceleration qE/m and bends sideways (Example 1.7).
hints: Between the plates a = qE/m. The drop crosses them in t = L/v₀, starting with no sideways speed.
The sideways shift is y = ½ a t². Solve for E.
A positive drop moves along the field, a negative drop against it. Choose the direction to send it to the target side.

levels.title: Track chamber
levels.adds: New idea: read tracks. The bend direction gives the sign, the size of the bend gives the charge-to-mass ratio (Ex 1.13).
hints: A positive particle bends the same way as the field; a negative one bends the opposite way.
All three enter at the same speed, so a bigger bend means a bigger q/m.
Fire all three and compare the tracks before you tag them.

levels.title: Long throw
levels.adds: Harder: the paper is beyond the plates, so the drop keeps moving sideways in a straight line after the field.
hints: Inside the plates, y₁ = ½ a t². At the exit the drop has sideways speed a t.
Over the gap D the drop travels straight and shifts a further a t D/v₀.
Add the two: y = (qE/m)(L/v₀²)(L/2 + D). Solve for E.

misconceptions: The field depends on the test charge
A negative charge moves along the field
A charged drop moves in a straight line through the plates
A heavier or more highly charged particle always bends more
